extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments, facility compliance managers, State and EPA regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and compliance guidance for owners/operators of legacy coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments under the finalized 40 CFR part 257, subpart D rule, including deadlines, reporting, monitoring, security, closure certifications, and extension procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance deadlines for legacy CCR surface impoundments (general framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: All deadlines are framed by reference to the effective date of the rule; the final rule will be effective six months after publication of the final rule. Facilities will have an additional six months beyond the deadlines to come into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA included a document in the docket summarizing finalized compliance deadlines. Deadlines in the table are expressed in months after the effective date and with calendar dates for reference. Where extensions are granted (see extension provisions), deadlines may be shifted unit-by-unit based on when an applicability report is prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability Report — completion required by effective date (§257.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an applicability report for any legacy CCR surface impoundment at that facility no later than the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicability report must include information to identify the unit, a figure of the facility and where the unit is located at the facility, and the current site conditions; facility address, latitude/longitude, and contact information for owner/operator; documentation whether impoundments are incised and whether units meet height/storage volume thresholds. Owner/operator must notify EPA of establishment of facility's CCR website using §257.107(a) procedures. The report must be certified (signed) by the owner/operator or an authorized representative (§257.100(f)(1)(ii)(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Posting — establish CCR website by effective date (§257.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a public CCR website for the facility by the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility must post specified documents (e.g., applicability reports, extension reports, certifications, notifications) to the CCR website as required by the rule and place certain documents in the operating record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Security — implement site security measures by effective date (§257.100(f)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish security controls to restrict access to legacy CCR surface impoundments by the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement is performance-based: prevent the unknowing entry of people onto the legacy CCR surface impoundment and minimize potential for unauthorized entry of people or livestock. Facility-wide access controls already in place satisfy the requirement. EPA modeled requirements on §265.14(a) interim hazardous waste impoundment controls. EPA finalizing proposed performance standard without revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — prepare fugitive dust control plan by effective date (§257.80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a fugitive dust control plan for the CCR unit by the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operating criterion required immediately (deadline = 0 months after effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — initiate weekly inspections of CCR unit (§257.80, 257.82, 257.83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin weekly inspections of the CCR unit by the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weekly inspection requirement begins immediately (deadline = 0 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — initiate monthly monitoring of CCR unit instrumentation (§257.80, 257.82, 257.83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin monthly monitoring of CCR unit instrumentation by the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly instrumentation monitoring requirement begins immediately (deadline = 0 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — install permanent identification marker (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Install a permanent marker on or immediately adjacent to the legacy impoundment no later than 2 months after the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicability extension is used (see extension rules), the deadline is adjusted by the amount of extension time; example provided showing calculation when an applicability determination is delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — complete initial annual inspection of the CCR unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete initial annual inspection of the CCR unit within 3 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial annual inspection deadline is 3 months after effective date (calendar example: Monday, February 10, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — complete initial annual fugitive dust report (§257.80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the initial annual fugitive dust report within 14 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial report deadline example: Thursday, January 8, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — compile history of construction (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile history of construction within 15 months after the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This activity (history of construction) will also tie into delineation of unit boundaries and other design determinations completed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — complete initial hazard potential classification assessment (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete an initial hazard potential classification assessment within 18 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline example: Friday, May 8, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — complete initial structural stability assessment (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete an initial structural stability assessment within 18 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same deadline window as hazard potential classification and safety factor assessment; supports emergency planning and design reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — complete initial safety factor assessment (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete an initial safety factor assessment within 18 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the design criteria package due in the 18-month timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Criteria — prepare emergency action plan (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an emergency action plan within 18 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency action plan is required alongside other design/assessment deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Criteria — complete initial inflow design flood control system plan (§257.82)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete initial inflow design flood control system plan within 18 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses flood control design for impoundment safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater Monitoring, Corrective Action (GWMCA) — install monitoring system and begin monitoring (§§257.90-257.95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Install the groundwater monitoring system, develop the groundwater sampling and analysis program, initiate detection and assessment monitoring, and begin evaluating groundwater monitoring data for statistically significant increases (SSIs) over background levels and statistically significant levels (SSLs) over groundwater protection standards within 30 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-month deadline example: Monday, May 10, 2027. Initial annual GWMCA report has its own January 31, 2027 date for the first annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: GWMCA — complete initial annual GWMCA report (§257.90(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete and submit the initial annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report by January 31, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual reporting schedule and content must follow §257.90(e) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure — prepare written closure plan (§§257.100-257.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a written closure plan within 36 months after the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline example: Monday, November 8, 2027. Closure planning must meet §257.101 performance standards and be completed in time to initiate closure per the schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Closure Care — prepare written post-closure care plan (§257.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a written post-closure care plan within 36 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-closure plan must address monitoring, maintenance, and long-term controls consistent with §257.104 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure and Post-Closure — initiate closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiate closure of the legacy CCR surface impoundment within 42 months after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar example: Monday, May 8, 2028. Initiation of closure triggers subsequent closure/post-closure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability extension report — eligibility and required parts (§257.100(f)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain more time to complete an applicability report, an owner/operator must prepare an applicability extension report by the effective date consisting of three parts: (1) general identifying information; (2) a statement that available information does not provide a sufficient basis to determine whether the impoundment contained free liquids on or after October 19, 2015; and (3) a written field investigation workplan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators that cannot truthfully make the required statement (i.e., they have evidence of free liquids) are not eligible for the extension. The extension report must be placed in the operating record and posted to the CCR website. The final rule allows up to three 6-month extensions (up to 18 months) — each additional extension requires a subsequent extension report prepared no later than six months after completing the preceding extension report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field investigation workplan — required elements (for extension reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written field investigation workplan must include: a detailed description of the approach to characterize physical/topographic/geologic/hydrogeologic/hydraulic properties; description of methods/tools and rationale and spatial resolution; description of how groundwater elevations will be determined and spatial resolution; plan for evaluating stormwater flow/drainage/infiltration with a current topographic map; estimated timeline to complete the workplan; narrative on how results will determine presence of free liquids; narrative on anticipated problems and contingencies with timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workplan should be sufficiently detailed to justify the need for extension time and to support the field investigation. Each 6-month extension must be supported by an updated extension report documenting progress and need for more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for applicability report after field determination of free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the owner/operator determines that an inactive impoundment contains CCR and liquids, the applicability report required by §257.100(f)(1) must be completed within 14 days of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After preparation of the applicability report, the unit becomes subject to legacy impoundment requirements under §257.100(f)(2)–(5) with compliance deadlines adjusted by the length of any extension used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination that a unit does not contain liquids — notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner/operator determines the unit does not contain liquids after the field investigation, they must prepare a notification stating that the field investigation concluded and that the unit does not contain CCR and liquids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification informs the public, States, and EPA that the unit is not a legacy CCR surface impoundment. If the owner/operator does not complete the field investigation within specified timeframes, the unit is considered a legacy CCR surface impoundment and must comply with all applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of closure by removal — supporting information required (§257.102(c) support)
rubrics_metrics.description: To certify that a legacy impoundment closed by removal in accordance with §257.102(c), the facility must support its certification with: (1) the type and volume of CCR and all other materials in the unit prior to closure; (2) the methods used to verify complete removal, including post-removal sampling and analysis; (3) documentation that all CCR and contaminated materials were removed, including results of post-removal sampling and analysis; (4) methods used to verify complete decontamination of affected areas, including post-decontamination sampling and analysis; and (5) documentation that affected areas were decontaminated and groundwater affected by releases has achieved groundwater protection standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identifies the minimum information needed to support a certification but does not substantially restrict the analyses or factual information that can be used. Certification must be supported by scientifically valid data that credibly demonstrate compliance with §257.102(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater data requirement for closure certification — Appendix IV constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: The facility must have groundwater monitoring data demonstrating that concentrations of each Appendix IV constituent do not exceed the relevant groundwater protection standard (either the MCL or background concentration) for two consecutive sampling events, consistent with §257.95(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many units closed before federal CCR groundwater monitoring requirements, EPA does not require the monitoring system to comply with all §§257.90–257.95 elements, but the data supporting certification must be scientifically valid and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum performance criteria for groundwater monitoring system used to support certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater monitoring system used to document Appendix IV constituent concentrations must have met a subset of performance standards in §§257.91(a)–(e), 257.93(a)–(d), and 257.93(i), specifically: (1) accurately represented background water quality unaffected by CCR unit; (2) accurately represented water quality passing the waste boundary; (3) capable of detecting contamination in the uppermost aquifer; (4) monitored all potential contaminant pathways; (5) established groundwater background concentrations and compared samples to background; and (6) utilized wells that are cased and maintained to protect borehole integrity, screened/perforated and packed as necessary, and sealed between borehole and casing to prevent contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The last sample used to demonstrate no Appendix IV constituent exceedances must have been collected no earlier than one year prior to initiation of closure. The system need not meet all modern CCR-specific monitoring system installation details, but must be capable and documented to reliably detect releases from the impoundment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification by qualified professional and timing for pre-effective-date closures
rubrics_metrics.description: For legacy CCR surface impoundments that completed closure by removal after October 19, 2015 but before the effective date, facilities must post documentation on their CCR website showing closure according to §257.102(c), and the closure certification must be certified by a qualified P.E.; certification placed in operating record no later than the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not accept blanket reliance on State-approved closures without supporting factual/legal bases. The rule identifies minimum required supporting documentation (see certification entry) to allow EPA/States/public to determine compliance with §257.102(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: When removal occurred earlier but monitoring absent — interim requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility removed all CCR prior to the effective date but did not conduct groundwater monitoring (or had noncompliant monitoring), the facility must install a groundwater monitoring system and initiate monitoring in accordance with §§257.90–257.95 as an initial requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the owner/operator elects to pursue closure certification, they must prepare a notification of intent to certify closure by the effective date, place it in the operating record, post it on the CCR website, and submit a notification to EPA or the State/Tribal Authority stating the facility has removed all CCR and will install monitoring to determine contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating record and public posting requirements (extensions, certifications, notifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension reports, applicability reports, closure certifications, notifications of intent, and similar documents must be placed in the facility's operating record and posted to the owner/operator's CCR website as required by the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each prepared extension report must be placed in the operating record as required §257.105(k)(2) and posted to CCR website. Closure certifications and related supporting documentation must also be placed in the operating record and posted to the CCR website by the effective date if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA's non-requirement decisions for applicability report content (size/proximity/delineation)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not requiring the applicability report to include the size of the unit, its proximity to surface water bodies, or delineation of unit boundaries because those will be determined through history of construction and groundwater monitoring requirements and were not feasible by the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found it infeasible to require these items by the effective date due to lack of historical records and the timing of delineation activities; proximity to surface water is not required by 2015 CCR Rule and is infeasible to determine before boundaries are delineated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'contains both CCR and liquids' and optional field investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes a definition for 'contains both CCR and liquids' — CCR and liquids are present except where owner/operator has demonstrated that free liquids have been eliminated consistent with the performance standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i). Facilities lacking records may elect to conduct a field investigation to assess presence/absence of free liquids; the rule provides procedures for additional time if facility elects field investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities are not required to conduct field testing if records permit determination; the extension procedure provides the option to conduct field investigations in lieu of relying solely on records.
